en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Dyad on the Visible (Sanidassanaduka)
A phenomenon that is both visible and impinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a phenomenon that is neither visible nor impinging.
(Abbreviated. There are three [types of conditions] in the case of the object; three in the case of predominance;
and three each in the cases of decisive support, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.

Dependent on a non-manifesting and impinging state that is non-manifesting, there arises a state that is neither non-manifesting nor impinging by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are nine [conditions] for root; nine for predominance … pe … nine for non-disappearance.
